signal.title: Real-Time Action Chunking with Large Models
signal.summary: 这项研究围绕视觉—语言—动作模型展开，关注机器人如何把视觉观察和语言指令，持续转换成跨时间的动作，而不是只对当前画面做一次反应。

editorial.intro: 这项研究围绕视觉—语言—动作模型展开，关注机器人如何把视觉观察和语言指令，持续转换成跨时间的动作，而不是只对当前画面做一次反应。
editorial.why_it_matters: VLA 的记忆、推理和实时执行能力，直接决定具身智能能否从演示动作走向长时任务和真实部署。
editorial.watch_next: 继续核对实验是否覆盖真实机器人、长时任务和跨场景泛化。

Galliker, Sergey Levine Paper Follow-Up Paper Update (Dec 8th, 2025): we released a follow-up paper describing a training-time version of RTC, which we used in the π * 0.6 espresso-making demo ! Loading… Unlike chatbots or image generators, robots must operate in real time . While a robot is “thinking”, the world around it
evolves according to physical laws, so delays between inputs and outputs have a tangible impact on performance. For a
language model, the difference between fast and slow generation is a satisfied or annoyed user; for a
vision-language-action model (VLA), it could be the difference between a robot handing you a hot coffee or spilling it in
your lap. While VLAs have achieved promising results in open-world
generalization, they can be slow to run. Like their cousins in language and vision, these models have billions of
parameters and require heavy-duty GPUs. On edge devices like mobile robots, that adds even more latency for network
